section_1.title: Vectors as Physical Movements
section_1.content: Introduce the prerequisite of the Cartesian coordinate system. Shift the perspective of a vector from a static 'list of numbers' to a dynamic 'arrow in space' representing displacement from the origin.
section_1.example: A small robot character starts at (0,0). The vector [3, 2] is shown as an arrow pushing the robot 3 units right and 2 units up, emphasizing direction and magnitude.

section_2.title: The DNA of Space: Basis Vectors
section_2.content: Explain that all space is built from 'i-hat' (unit vector on x-axis) and 'j-hat' (unit vector on y-axis). Every vector is just a combination (linear combination) of these two fundamental building blocks.
section_2.example: Visualizing i-hat as a red arrow (1,0) and j-hat as a green arrow (0,1). The vector [3, -2] is animated as '3 copies of red' and '-2 copies of green' being added together.

section_3.title: Transformation: Morphing the Grid
section_3.content: Introduce a Linear Transformation not as a formula, but as a 'warp' of space. Define the rules: the origin must remain fixed, and all grid lines must remain parallel and evenly spaced.
section_3.example: A picture of a 'Square Cat' sitting on a standard grid. As a matrix is applied, the entire grid (and the cat) stretches and slants into a parallelogram shape, showing space itself morphing.

section_4.title: Decoding the Matrix: Where do the Basis Vectors land?
section_4.content: The 'Aha!' moment. Explain that the columns of a 2x2 matrix are simply the coordinates of where i-hat and j-hat landed after the transformation. This links the numbers directly to the visual change.
section_4.example: A matrix [ [2, 1], [-1, 1] ]. We track the red arrow (i-hat) landing at (2, -1) and the green arrow (j-hat) landing at (1, 1). The 'new' space is instantly defined by these two landing spots.

section_5.title: The Determinant: Scaling the Area
section_5.content: Define the determinant geometrically. It is the factor by which areas are scaled during the transformation. If the area of a unit square becomes 6, the determinant is 6.
section_5.example: A gold 1x1 square is shown before the transformation. After the space slants, the square becomes a larger parallelogram. The animation calculates the new area, showing how a determinant of 0 would 'squish' all of 2D space into a 1D line.

outline.title: Vectors as Physical Movements
outline.content: Introduce the prerequisite of the Cartesian coordinate system. Shift the perspective of a vector from a static 'list of numbers' to a dynamic 'arrow in space' representing displacement from the origin.
outline.example: A small robot character starts at (0,0). The vector [3, 2] is shown as an arrow pushing the robot 3 units right and 2 units up, emphasizing direction and magnitude.

outline.title: The DNA of Space: Basis Vectors
outline.content: Explain that all space is built from 'i-hat' (unit vector on x-axis) and 'j-hat' (unit vector on y-axis). Every vector is just a combination (linear combination) of these two fundamental building blocks.
outline.example: Visualizing i-hat as a red arrow (1,0) and j-hat as a green arrow (0,1). The vector [3, -2] is animated as '3 copies of red' and '-2 copies of green' being added together.

storyboard.title: Vectors as Physical Movements
lecture_lines: Start with a standard Cartesian coordinate system.
Think of a vector as a movement through space.
An arrow from the origin shows direction and distance.
animations: Show a faint white (#FFFFFF) coordinate grid on black background.
Place a small white (#FFFFFF) circle representing a robot at origin.
Draw a bold blue (#0000FF) arrow from (0,0) to (3,2).
Animate robot moving 3 units right, then 2 units up.
Label the arrow '[3, 2]' in blue (#0000FF) at its tip.

storyboard.title: The DNA of Space: Basis Vectors
lecture_lines: Every 2D vector is built from two fundamental pieces.
i-hat is a unit vector along the x-axis.
j-hat is a unit vector along the y-axis.
Combine these scaled pieces to reach any point.
These basic building blocks are called basis vectors.
animations: Show red (#FF0000) i-hat and green (#00FF00) j-hat from origin.
Scale i-hat 3x right; scale j-hat 2x downwards.
Move scaled j-hat to tip of scaled i-hat, forming [3,-2].

outline.title: Decoding the Matrix: Where do the Basis Vectors land?
outline.content: The 'Aha!' moment. Explain that the columns of a 2x2 matrix are simply the coordinates of where i-hat and j-hat landed after the transformation. This links the numbers directly to the visual change.
outline.example: A matrix [ [2, 1], [-1, 1] ]. We track the red arrow (i-hat) landing at (2, -1) and the green arrow (j-hat) landing at (1, 1). The 'new' space is instantly defined by these two landing spots.

storyboard.title: Decoding the Matrix: Where do the Basis Vectors land?
lecture_lines: A matrix tells us where basis vectors land.
The first column shows i-hat's new position.
The second column shows j-hat's new position.
These two landing spots define the transformed space.
Numbers in the matrix now have a geometric meaning.
animations: Display a 2x2 matrix with columns highlighted in red/green.
Animate i-hat (red) moving to (2,-1) and j-hat (green) to (1,1).
Overlay the transformed grid defined by these new vector positions.

outline.title: The Determinant: Scaling the Area
outline.content: Define the determinant geometrically. It is the factor by which areas are scaled during the transformation. If the area of a unit square becomes 6, the determinant is 6.
outline.example: A gold 1x1 square is shown before the transformation. After the space slants, the square becomes a larger parallelogram. The animation calculates the new area, showing how a determinant of 0 would 'squish' all of 2D space into a 1D line.

storyboard.title: The Determinant: Scaling the Area
lecture_lines: Determinants measure how much space is scaled.
Look at the area of a single unit square.
The transformation stretches or squishes this area.
This area scaling factor is the determinant.
A determinant of zero collapses space into a line.
animations: Highlight a gold (#FFD700) 1x1 unit square at the origin.
Transform space; show the square morphing into a parallelogram.
Label the new area with the value of the determinant.
Perform a second transformation that flattens the grid into a line.
Flash the determinant value '0' as the area disappears.

section_1.title: Vectors as Physical Movements
section_1.content: Introduce the prerequisite of the Cartesian coordinate system. Shift the perspective of a vector from a static 'list of numbers' to a dynamic 'arrow in space' representing displacement from the origin.
section_1.example: A small robot character starts at (0,0). The vector [3, 2] is shown as an arrow pushing the robot 3 units right and 2 units up, emphasizing direction and magnitude.

section_2.title: The DNA of Space: Basis Vectors
section_2.content: Explain that all space is built from 'i-hat' (unit vector on x-axis) and 'j-hat' (unit vector on y-axis). Every vector is just a combination (linear combination) of these two fundamental building blocks.
section_2.example: Visualizing i-hat as a red arrow (1,0) and j-hat as a green arrow (0,1). The vector [3, -2] is animated as '3 copies of red' and '-2 copies of green' being added together.

section_3.title: Transformation: Morphing the Grid
section_3.content: Introduce a Linear Transformation not as a formula, but as a 'warp' of space. Define the rules: the origin must remain fixed, and all grid lines must remain parallel and evenly spaced.
section_3.example: A picture of a 'Square Cat' sitting on a standard grid. As a matrix is applied, the entire grid (and the cat) stretches and slants into a parallelogram shape, showing space itself morphing.

section_4.title: Decoding the Matrix: Where do the Basis Vectors land?
section_4.content: The 'Aha!' moment. Explain that the columns of a 2x2 matrix are simply the coordinates of where i-hat and j-hat landed after the transformation. This links the numbers directly to the visual change.
section_4.example: A matrix [ [2, 1], [-1, 1] ]. We track the red arrow (i-hat) landing at (2, -1) and the green arrow (j-hat) landing at (1, 1). The 'new' space is instantly defined by these two landing spots.

section_5.title: The Determinant: Scaling the Area
section_5.content: Define the determinant geometrically. It is the factor by which areas are scaled during the transformation. If the area of a unit square becomes 6, the determinant is 6.
section_5.example: A gold 1x1 square is shown before the transformation. After the space slants, the square becomes a larger parallelogram. The animation calculates the new area, showing how a determinant of 0 would 'squish' all of 2D space into a 1D line.

outline.content: Explain that all space is built from 'i-hat' (unit vector on x-axis) and 'j-hat' (unit vector on y-axis). Every vector is just a combination (linear combination) of these two fundamental building blocks.
outline.example: Visualizing i-hat as a red arrow (1,0) and j-hat as a green arrow (0,1). The vector [3, -2] is animated as '3 copies of red' and '-2 copies of green' being added together.

i-hat is a unit vector along the x-axis.
j-hat is a unit vector along the y-axis.
Combine these scaled pieces to reach any point.
These basic building blocks are called basis vectors.
animations: Show the origin with a faint white (#FFFFFF) grid in the background.
Draw a red (#FF0000) unit vector 'i-hat' from (0,0) to (1,0) along the x-axis.
Draw a green (#00FF00) unit vector 'j-hat' from (0,0) to (0,1) along the y-axis.
Scale red (#FF0000) i-hat 3x and green (#00FF00) j-hat -2x, then sum them tip-to-tail.
Flash the labels 'i-hat' (red #FF0000) and 'j-hat' (green #00FF00) to identify them as basis vectors.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

            "i-hat is a unit vector along the x-axis.",
            "j-hat is a unit vector along the y-axis.",
            "Combine these scaled pieces to reach any point.",
            "These basic building blocks are called basis vectors."

        COLOR_I = "#FF0000"
        COLOR_J = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_V = "#FFFFFF"
        HIGHLIGHT = YELLOW
        
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lecture_lines_str)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT))
        
        # Coordinate Plane
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-1, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 2, 1],
            x_length=3,
            y_length=3,
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.3}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, "B2", "E5")
        
        self.play(Create(plane))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_I)
        )

        i_tip = plane.coords_to_point(1, 0)
        i_hat = Arrow(origin, i_tip, buff=0, color=COLOR_I, stroke_width=4)
        # Using Text instead of MathTex to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        i_hat_label = Text("î", color=COLOR_I, font_size=20)
        i_hat_label.next_to(i_hat, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(i_hat), Write(i_hat_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_J)
        )

        j_hat = Arrow(origin, j_tip, buff=0, color=COLOR_J, stroke_width=4)
        j_hat_label = Text("ĵ", color=COLOR_J, font_size=20)
        j_hat_label.next_to(j_hat, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(j_hat), Write(j_hat_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_V)
        )
        
        # Scaling i-hat by 3
        i_scaled_tip = plane.coords_to_point(3, 0)
        i_scaled = Arrow(origin, i_scaled_tip, buff=0, color=COLOR_I, stroke_width=4)
        i_scaled_label = Text("3î", color=COLOR_I, font_size=20)
        i_scaled_label.next_to(i_scaled, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Scaling j-hat by -2
        j_scaled_tip = plane.coords_to_point(0, -2)
        j_scaled = Arrow(origin, j_scaled_tip, buff=0, color=COLOR_J, stroke_width=4)
        j_scaled_label = Text("-2ĵ", color=COLOR_J, font_size=20)
        j_scaled_label.next_to(j_scaled, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(i_hat, i_scaled),
            ReplacementTransform(i_hat_label, i_scaled_label),
            ReplacementTransform(j_hat, j_scaled),
            ReplacementTransform(j_hat_label, j_scaled_label)
        )
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Move j_scaled to tip of i_scaled
        shift_vector = i_scaled_tip - origin
        self.play(
            j_scaled.animate.shift(shift_vector),
            j_scaled_label.animate.shift(shift_vector)
        )
        
        # Resultant vector [3, -2]
        res_tip = plane.coords_to_point(3, -2)
        v_res = Arrow(origin, res_tip, buff=0, color=COLOR_V, stroke_width=6)
        v_label = Text("v = 3î - 2ĵ", color=COLOR_V, font_size=20)
        v_label.next_to(v_res.get_end(), DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(Create(v_res), Write(v_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT)
        )
        
        basis_tag = Text("Basis Vectors", font_size=20, color=HIGHLIGHT)
        self.place_at_grid(basis_tag, "A4")
        
        self.play(
            Indicate(i_scaled, color=COLOR_I),
            Indicate(j_scaled, color=COLOR_J),
            Write(basis_tag)
        )
        
        self.wait(3)
